original_question: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional Martinet distribution, consider a sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q_0 and a point where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve. What is the C^1-classification, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of R^3, of the germ of the sphere at such a point?
target_in_paper: Section IV, "Unfolding the sub-Riemannian distance": the unnumbered open question, stated after the Martinet flat-case example, asking for a C^1-classification of the germs of sub-Riemannian spheres at points of optimal singular curves for generic metrics, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of ℝ^3. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right local setting (Martinet, dimension 3), the right object (the germ of a sub-Riemannian sphere rather than the whole distance function), the right locus (a point where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve), and the right equivalence relation (ambient C^1-equivalence via germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of ℝ^3). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
missing_details: The paper is explicitly local: one works near a Martinet point q0 and with a sufficiently small sphere S_{q0}(ε), so that the question concerns germs and short optimal singular segments. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The Martinet hypothesis should be spelled out in the paper’s terms: a rank-2 distribution Δ in ℝ^3 near q0 with n2(q0)=2 and n3(q0)=3 (equivalently, Δ^2 has rank 2 and Δ^3 has rank 3 at q0). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The paper’s nearby context identifies the Martinet surface Σ={q : n2(q)=2}, states that Δ is transverse to Σ, and explains that singular curves are exactly the integral curves of the line field Δ∩TΣ; these are the singular curves whose small segments are optimal. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

For the sphere to meet an optimal singular curve issuing from the center, q0 should be understood as a Martinet point in the above sense; this is implicit in the paper’s setup. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The paper phrases the problem for generic metrics on the given Martinet distribution; it does not ask for a classification across all 3-dimensional sub-Riemannian structures or for the Engel and higher-dimensional analogues discussed immediately afterward. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
refined_question: Let Δ⊂Tℝ^3 be a rank-2 Martinet distribution near a point q0, meaning that Δ^2:=Δ+[Δ,Δ] has rank 2 at q0 and Δ^3:=Δ^2+[Δ,Δ^2] has rank 3 at q0; let Σ={q near q0 : rank Δ^2_q=2} be the Martinet surface, so that Δ is transverse to Σ and the singular curves are exactly the integral curves of the line field Δ∩TΣ, whose sufficiently short segments are optimal. For a generic sub-Riemannian metric g on Δ, fix ε>0 sufficiently small and let S_{q0}(ε) be the corresponding sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q0. If q∈S_{q0}(ε) lies on an optimal singular curve issuing from q0, determine the C^1-equivalence class of the germ of S_{q0}(ε) at q, where two germs are identified when they are related by a germ of a C^1-diffeomorphism of ℝ^3. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper, but the exact target is not a numbered conjecture/proposition/theorem: arXiv:1304.2590 states this as an unnumbered open question in §IV. Agrachev first sets up the Martinet case by requiring n2(q0)=2 and n3(q0)=3, defines the Martinet surface and its singular line field, recalls the flat model, and then asks for a C^1-classification of sphere germs at points of optimal singular curves for generic metrics. The refined version above keeps that scope, adds the local hypotheses and notation that the paper leaves implicit in the one-sentence question, and avoids drifting into the Engel and higher-dimensional generalizations that come immediately afterward. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
